transcript_tail.text: All 4 AH siblings are present (as same-dir siblings inside each source's bridge-worktree project dir — no `--into-main` was used). Now the DST one — its mark used `--mark-text` so the uuid isn't in the title.

DST source has no project dir on note (its bridge worktree lives on mini, which is exactly why it shows `other-host`). The sibling, if any, would either be on mini or — if `--into-main` was used — in note's main-checkout project dir for that repo. Checking both possibilities.

Tally of existing siblings:

| Source (cse_…) | Sibling on note? | Path |
|---|---|---|
| `…01UosQJUfmip9nh8oJFxdqvQ` | yes | `~/.claude/projects/…bridge-cse-01UosQJUfmip9nh8oJFxdqvQ/eb8a0d62-fe49-4b12-b7e0-8d003dd8bfef.jsonl` |
| `…01KEWoeHzSKtc3YEiNRgKDxj` | yes | `~/.claude/projects/…bridge-cse-01KEWoeHzSKtc3YEiNRgKDxj/999be634-bb85-42a9-9dd3-c070ac2a87f1.jsonl` |
| `…01XtFhCtBTr4fEzBmXVUdFgj` | yes | `~/.claude/projects/…bridge-cse-01XtFhCtBTr4fEzBmXVUdFgj/af2a953b-29ef-44c2-af30-3807b2582253.jsonl` |
| `…01GKTKEfm7DPDj1BVvoSRPLB` | yes | `~/.claude/projects/…bridge-cse-01GKTKEfm7DPDj1BVvoSRPLB/1b330640-7162-4115-9019-f7946c4711b2.jsonl` |
| `…0143ii5b4T6NXNZ9B9FhdRtC` (DST) | **not on note** | source dir doesn't exist here; sibling (if any) is on mini |

Observations:

- **All four AH siblings exist as same-dir siblings** (no `--into-main` was used — they sit inside the bridge-worktree project dir of their source, not in `-Users-claudio1-dev-ai-harness`).
- **None of the AH sources need re-forking** — every one has a present, resumable sibling. Re-running `fork-all` against them would just produce a second copy of the same transcript with a new uuid.
- **The DST one is opaque from note.** Its source bridge dir lives on mini, so its sibling (if `--mark` was paired with a real fork) is on mini's `~/.claude/projects/`. From here you can't tell whether the `→ clean-repo prep` mark accompanied a real fork or was set via `--mark-text` without one.

So the safe answer to "can we re-fork using `fork-all`": yes the command works (modulo dropping `--host`), but the 4 AH ids in your screenshot don't need it, and the DST id needs a check from mini before you decide.

If you want, next step is one of:
1. **Archive the 4 AH sources only** (the local siblings already exist; no re-fork needed) — `python3 -m remote_control sessions archive cse_01UosQJUfmip9nh8oJFxdqvQ cse_01KEWoeHzSKtc3YEiNRgKDxj cse_01XtFhCtBTr4fEzBmXVUdFgj cse_01GKTKEfm7DPDj1BVvoSRPLB --dry-run`.
2. **SSH/run on mini to check the DST sibling**, then decide DST separately.
3. **Force a fresh re-fork of all 5** anyway (you'll get a second sibling per source).

Which?
I cannot see the sibling sessions? how can I find them? are they active? can we refork?

Three clean answers:

**1. Why you can't see them.** `sessions list` is **cloud-only** — it calls `monitor.list_sessions()` which hits the Anthropic API. The 4 siblings are **local** sessions (uuid-shaped, no `cse_` id), so the cloud doesn't know they exist. There's no harness command that lists local sessions today; you find them on disk:

```
ls -lt ~/.claude/projects/*bridge-cse-*/*.jsonl
```

…or in `claude`'s own `/resume` UI if you launch from the right cwd.

**2. Are they active?** No. The 4 jsonls were last written **today between 18:44 and 18:48** (when fork ran), and **no `claude` process holds them right now**. They are inert transcripts. A local sibling only becomes "active" when you resume it: `cd <bridge worktree> && claude -r <uuid>`. To wake them up:

```
(cd ~/dev/ai-harness/.claude/worktrees/bridge-cse_01UosQJUfmip9nh8oJFxdqvQ && claude -r eb8a0d62-fe49-4b12-b7e0-8d003dd8bfef)
(cd ~/dev/ai-harness/.claude/worktrees/bridge-cse_01KEWoeHzSKtc3YEiNRgKDxj && claude -r 999be634-bb85-42a9-9dd3-c070ac2a87f1)
(cd ~/dev/ai-harness/.claude/worktrees/bridge-cse_01XtFhCtBTr4fEzBmXVUdFgj && claude -r af2a953b-29ef-44c2-af30-3807b2582253)
(cd ~/dev/ai-harness/.claude/worktrees/bridge-cse_01GKTKEfm7DPDj1BVvoSRPLB && claude -r 1b330640-7162-4115-9019-f7946c4711b2)
```

(For the DST one, the sibling — if any — is on mini; can't resume it from note.)

**3. Can we re-fork?** Yes — `do_fork` mints a fresh uuid every call and writes a new `<uuid>.jsonl` next to the existing one. The old siblings are not touched, just stranded. So safe to do, but you'll end up with **two** siblings per AH source (the old May-25-18:44 ones and the new ones).
